whether the document is kept true, preserved as written, or derived from measurement

who keeps the document true; a bare row is counted by the registry rather than hidden

the one thing that breaks if the test is deleted; blanks are counted

how many assertions the file makes. Blank, never zero, on the 10 browser-driven checks that are not node:test files, because test() is not their unit; the blank is the honest reading and the count is the ledger figure

what each top-level test() call is named, in source order; the file's own account of its coverage, so protects need not restate it. A parameterized name is carried as its template text. Blank on the same 10 browser-driven checks as its count, for the same reason: test() is not their unit
how the check reaches its subject, strongest present wins
suite for a *.test.mjs file, else the npm script that runs it, else unrun

which assertions only check a component mounts, as indices into assertion_names; the property is per assertion, so a file-level count is the length rather than the record. Blank on the same 10 browser-driven checks, for the same reason
what the file is for; blanks are counted rather than hidden
which shelf the file sits on. The domain is closed and owned by the carrier's own layers glossary block, the same arrangement as manifest-fields.consumer; docs/code-layers.md is the prose behind it
file length

how the file gets run: argv, imported, driver, 'none found' (the warning state), or npm:<script> naming the script. Deliberately OPEN, because the npm form is a grammar rather than an enumeration and a new script must not need a declaration edit
writes a file: a generator rather than a reader

a file under tools/test/ exercises it

the invocation name; present on kind:skill rows only

how a consumer takes the item: installed by the plugin, read live, referenced, adopted once, or fetched on demand
